title: The Lord's Will Be Done
excerpt: Acts 21:1–16 | A marked man sails toward Jerusalem and the chains he knows are waiting — warned by the Spirit at every port. But the hardest lesson falls on the people who love him, who must open their hands and pray what Jesus prayed first: not my will, but yours.

title: Leaving Like Jesus Left
excerpt: Acts 20:32–38 | A beach, a ship, a crowd of grown men weeping. Paul leaves the way Jesus left — open hands, holding nothing in a clenched fist: not silver, not ministry, not even the people he loves. The open hand isn't loss; it's the freest way a life gets shaped like his.

title: The Shepherd's Love
excerpt: Acts 20:25–31 | The flock was bought with the blood of God himself — that price hangs on every face in the room. Paul's last charge to weary shepherds: love is the only credential, love is what stays when the wolf comes, and the blood is the measure of what they were worth.

title: Finish The Race
excerpt: Acts 20:17–24 | Paul looks both ways down his race — costly service behind, chains ahead — and runs on. The finish line isn't a place; it's a Person. And at this table we take the cup of the One who finished first, poured out for us — bread and cup for the road, until we cross the line.

title: Life In The Room
excerpt: Acts 20:1–12 | Luke is telling Paul's story over Jesus' story on purpose. And the first scene is already Easter: resurrection day, broken bread, an upper room, and a boy who falls to his death and is carried out alive. You are that boy.

title: Little Man, Limitless Horizon
excerpt: Acts 19:21–22 | His name meant 'little' — a tentmaker with no army, no throne, about to be chased out by a mob. Yet he said, 'I must see Rome.' The smallest man in the empire carried the largest dream in history, because the love of Christ compelled him.

title: Manufactured Outrage
excerpt: Acts 19:23–41 | A whole city chants as one for two hours — and most don't even know why. The loudest unity the world can build is often its emptiest: a Babel of made gods and manufactured outrage. The gospel walks in and exposes the hollow centre.

title: Borrowed Credentials
excerpt: Acts 19:13–20 | Seven men tried to use the name of Jesus like a magic password — and it ended in disaster. The Name isn't a formula you can borrow; it's a Person you belong to. Don't brandish his name — bow to the One who gave it.

title: The Borrowed Room
excerpt: Acts 19:8–10 | When the synagogue hardened and shut its doors, Paul didn't stall — he rented a lecture hall and kept going. A hardened heart can close a door, but it can never stop the word of God. From one borrowed, ordinary room, a whole province heard.

title: Have You Received
excerpt: Acts 19:1–7 | Paul asks one question that exposes a half-built faith: have you received the Holy Spirit? Not as an upgrade. Not a second blessing. There's no such thing as a partial Christian — the Spirit-filled life is the only one there is.

title: The Road So Far
excerpt: From a worship service in Antioch to a kitchen table in Ephesus, the gospel never stopped moving. Explore Paul’s first two missionary journeys — the cities, the cost, the grace, the people — and discover where you are in a story that’s still being written.

title: More Accurately
excerpt: Acts 18:18–28 | Paul completes his vow and sails away. The camera stays with the seed he planted. A man from Alexandria had everything except the full story. Two refugees took him home and gave him Pentecost. The church grows at kitchen tables, not just on stages.

title: I Have People Here
excerpt: Acts 18:9–11 | Paul arrived at his greatest assignment afraid. Then God spoke into the dark: don't be afraid, keep speaking, I am with you. For everyone who's been faithful and is running on empty.

title: East to West
excerpt: Acts 18:1–9 | God's purposes don't go around. They cut through — through empires, through expulsion, through the walls that close. The Gospel has always taken the shortest line between where it is and where it needs to be.

title: Wanted
excerpt: Acts 17:22–34 | The God you've been reaching for has been standing right next to you the whole time — and He didn't come because He needed you. He came because He wanted you.

title: The Gospel In The Marketplace
excerpt: Acts 17:16–34 | Athens had a thousand answers already. What it didn't have was a God who had actually done something. Paul didn't walk in with a philosophy. He walked in with Good News.

title: readme.bible
excerpt: Acts 17:10–15 | The Bereans didn't just believe Paul. They went home and checked. Day after day they opened the text and cross-examined every claim. God's Word held up under every question they brought to it.

title: Guilty As Charged
excerpt: Acts 17:5–9 | The mob at Thessalonica meant their charges as an indictment. Every single one of them was true. They accidentally wrote the most faithful summary of the Gospel in Acts. The prosecution made the case for the defense — and Luke knew exactly what he was doing when he wrote it down.

title: My Resurrected Life
excerpt: Acts 17:1-5 | He suffered — so you are not alone in your pain. He died — so you carry no debt. He rose — and because he rose, so did you. Resurrection is not the last chapter. It's the one you're in right now. You are not waiting to be raised. In Christ, you already are. Live like it.

title: Citizens of Heaven
excerpt: Acts 16:34-40 | Your citizenship is in heaven. Your victory is secured. Your identity is already established. That joy is yours to live in today. You're not waiting. You already are. So live like it.

title: Believe In Jesus
excerpt: Acts 16:31 | The answer to the most important question a human being can ask is one sentence long. Not a course. Not a checklist. Not a better version of yourself first. Just this: believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved.

title: We Are All Here
excerpt: Acts 16:25–26 | They were beaten, chained, and locked in the deepest cell. And at midnight — they started singing. Before the doors opened. Before the chains fell. Before anything changed. This is what worship looks like when it costs everything.

title: Mind Your Business
excerpt: Acts 16:19–24 | The girl walked free. Now we look at the men who owned her — and what happened when God disrupted their income. A Kingdom audit of how we work, lead, spend, and build.

title: Net Worth
excerpt: Acts 16:16–24 | A girl with no name. Only a function. Her masters saw a profit — Paul saw a soul. Seven words later, everything changed. What does it mean to carry the Image of God in a world that only deals in assets?

title: Open Heart. Open Home.
excerpt: Acts 16:13–15 | Lydia's (Acts 16) Living Room church isn't a modern experiment; it's the restoration of an ancient pattern.

title: The Open Road
excerpt: Acts 16:10–13 | The infrastructure of the world is often the very road God uses to carry the peace of His Kingdom.

title: Red Light. Green Light.
excerpt: Acts 16:6–15 | We all know the frustration of being stopped when we were ready to move. Learning to move with the Spirit in seasons of waiting.
